residualRemoved.whatItWas: The previous wave repaired a leaf that names NONE of the host's builtins AUTOMATICALLY, and documented the residual: a user who DELIBERATELY removes every builtin is byte-identical to that damage and would be repaired once more.
residualRemoved.whyGuessingWasWrong: The two states are the same bytes, so any automatic rule must either overwrite a real choice or leave real damage — there is no third option. The boundary is therefore removed by NOT guessing: the automatic path never overrules an existing list, and the repair becomes an act only a human can request.
newRules: AUTOMATIC: an ABSENT leaf is seeded from the host's own current default (read from the installed module; the run REFUSES if it cannot be read).
AUTOMATIC: an EXISTING leaf is a POSITION and is returned BYTE-FOR-BYTE — including one that names none of the builtins. No residual: nothing automatic can ever touch it.
EXPLICIT: `--restore-builtins` is the ONE path that puts missing builtins back. It is a flag, not an inference.
residualRemoved.noResidualLeft: The only remaining way the builtins can be absent is that the user (or the host's own /settings UI) put them absent — and the tool now leaves that alone by construction.

implementation.resolvePanelSeed: reduced to TWO cases — absent leaf -> the host default; existing leaf -> itself. The 'all builtins missing' branch was DELETED.

implementation.options: `--restore-builtins` added to the option parser and to the usage block.
implementation.earlyExit: the 'already enabled' return still requires `restored.length === 0`, so an explicit restore is never swallowed (proved below: the sandbox `--apply` WROTE).
implementation.header: the file header now states both rules and why the repair is explicit.
